extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting, sustaining, and revising narrative point of view and developing an author's distinct voice across a manuscript. Covers POV rules, voice identification, voice layers, and revision techniques to preserve voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sphere of Knowledge (POV)
rubrics_metrics.description: POV is fundamentally about "sphere of knowledge" — narrator has specific knowledge limits that differ from author and characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the narrator's knowledge, perceptions, and access to information remain within a coherent sphere; avoid letting authorial knowledge slip into a narrator or character in ways that violate the chosen POV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep POV consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep it consistent — once you pick a lane, stay in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not switch POV types arbitrarily within scenes or chapters; consistency helps reader immersion and prevents confusion. If you change POV, do so with clear structural signals (e.g., chapter breaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep POV sustainable
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep it sustainable — works throughout the entire manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a POV that you can maintain for the length of the book; test whether the chosen perspective can deliver necessary plot information, emotional depth, and variety without strain or awkward contortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep POV real (observe conventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep it real — understand realistic conventions of each POV form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the expectations and limits of first person, close third, omniscient, etc., and follow or deliberately subvert those conventions with awareness. Understand what readers typically accept from each POV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice as literary DNA
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice as Literary DNA. Rather than something to "find," voice is your unique creative expression that already exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat voice as inherent to the writer; cultivate and reveal it rather than forcing it. Pereira's metaphor: voice is a sunflower seed — you can't make it grow roses. Use that mindset to avoid trying to manufacture a voice that doesn't fit you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name your voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Name Your Voice. Identify your voice's characteristics. Pereira's: "Professor Valley Girl" — knowledgeable but approachable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a shorthand persona or label for your voice to clarify traits you want to emphasize (tone, register, humor, authority). Use this label while drafting/revising to keep voice consistent and intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize multiple voice layers
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple Voice Layers: character voices (how individuals speak); narrator's voice (story's telling perspective); meta voice (in stories within stories); author's voice (distinct expression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that voice operates at multiple levels and make deliberate choices for each layer so they complement rather than clash. Ensure character dialogue, the narrator's narration, any embedded story voice, and the author's stylistic tendencies are distinct and serve the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reboot scenes rather than edit
rubrics_metrics.description: Reboot Scenes Rather Than Edit — Rewrite from memory; preserves authentic voice and energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a scene feels flat or off-voice, try rewriting it from memory instead of line-editing. This can help recover the original energy and keep the voice fresh and authentic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use TK markers for revision
rubrics_metrics.description: TK Markers — Insert "TK" (rare letter combo) to mark changes for easy search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a visible, easy-to-search marker like 'TK' to flag places needing later revision or replacement so you can maintain drafting flow without losing track of issues to fix.
